# Cooperative Election Study (CES): agent index

A large online survey of U.S. adults about elections and politics, run by YouGov since 2006 (as the CCES until 2020), with a common-content file per year and a cumulative file that harmonizes the years.

Publisher: Cooperative Election Study (Harvard Dataverse). Dataset id: `ces`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year.

Tables in `cumulative`: the key identifies a row; a reference says which columns join to another table, and when.

- `cumulative`: The cumulative common content (cumulative_2006-2025.dta), one row per respondent per year. Key: year, case_id

Tables in `2020`: the key identifies a row; a reference says which columns join to another table, and when.

- `common`: The 2020 common content (CES20_Common_OUTPUT_vv.dta). Key: caseid

- `common`: The 2022 common content (CCES22_Common_OUTPUT_vv_topost.dta). Key: caseid

- `common`: The 2024 common content (CCES24_Common_OUTPUT_vv_topost_final.dta). Key: caseid

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `cumulative`: 2006-2025; `2020`: 2020; `2022`: 2022; `2024`: 2024. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.

## Across releases

One line per variable across all releases, joined by the links between releases: names and the releases each had ("ADDEPEV2 2011–2018 → ADDEPEV3 2019–2023"). A change of meaning (codes, wording or universe) gives a second line, marked ↳, under the first. Search by subject, group or release in the shards above; use this to see how a variable runs across releases.
